stagePresence: Shy

achievements: Taking a singles tournament at the Shediac legion.
strengths: Scoring
dartSetup: 26 g windmau flights
practiceRoutine: Playing games with different people with higher averages.
checkouts: Love double 32
currentForm: Confident

achievements: Previously made the NB team in 2003, 2004 and 2005. After 19 years away I returned to darts and won 1st place ladies single at Cocagne. Made NB team in 2024 (5th) and 2025 (4th). In 2026 clinched 1st place for team NB - my proudest achievement!
strengths: If I can get in a good flow I can find myself shooting scores of 100+ back to back. I prefer leaving myself with dbl 16 or dbl 20.
improvements: My stance and the way I throw. Sometimes my arm is not locked in where it should be. Also my mindset on certain situations and figuring out my best option for a double out. Always learning!
dartSetup: Harrows Power Points (hammer heads) 22g, Mission force 90 moulded flight and shaft medium. My first and only set of darts!
practiceRoutine: I practice my doubles starting from dbl 20 all the way down to the bull. I sometimes time myself. If I have more time I try to hit each double 5 times before moving to the next. Then I'll hit the main triples and play a game of 501 or 170.
checkouts: I try not to limit myself to only a specific double as it always changes for me. I finished a 154 at NB tryouts, and I'm still trying to get that 170 finish - it's my goal!
currentForm: I'm super excited for this event! I'm making sure I'm hitting the board and getting the rhythm of my throw to be at my best on May 30th!
recentResults: Won the Ladies Single NB Port City open last September. Lost against Darlene McCloud at the Nova Scotia open in November.
mentalApproach: Mostly calm and focused, but sometimes aggressive at the start of a leg to set the tone.
pressureManagement: I try to stay calm and focus on what I need to get done. Pretty much tell myself you got this, one dart at a time.
stagePresence: On stage I'm mostly focused on the board. I try to block out the crowd. Just me
preMatchRituals: the board and my opponent.
aadsMeaning: I keep my arm warmed up before the game and stay mentally tough, reminding myself I'm a really good player and I can beat anyone.

achievements: I'm super proud of competing with team NB in 2025, and getting to go again this year.
strengths: Lately, scoring for me has come a long way. A lot of studying numbers and learning the math really made my game step up. Knowing the board is HUGE.
improvements: I think everyone can always work on nailing those doubles. That's usually a big focus for me.
dartSetup: 23g Karrah Kennedy Princess darts with 41mm points, and caliburn tweeny flights. Recently made the switch to somewhat longer points.
practiceRoutine: No specific routine YET! Just beating Adam at the moment.
checkouts: No
currentForm: Definitely finding my rhythm right now. Confidence is building!
recentResults: Not lately. It's gonna come though!!!
pressureManagement: Working on staying positive through the entire match. It's not over until that last double is hit, every single dart matters. I've been focusing more on my side of the scoreboard and not what my opponent is doing.
stagePresence: Trying to stay focused on the board more.
preMatchRituals: I have to find a specific spot on the oche for my foot. After each throw, trying to look down at my feet and not the opponent's throw or score.
hobbies: I coach high school volleyball, play women's volleyball and coed softball. Love hunting and fishing!
aadsMeaning: I'm very excited and honoured to be chosen to compete in this event! We've followed a lot of the AADS men's events and I've been waiting for the day we get to join in on the action!

achievements: 2025 Nova Scotia Provincial Champ. 2024 and 2025 World Masters Invitations. 170 checkout!
strengths: Composure and clutch finishing. Friends have coined me as "3rd Dart Jo" for often hitting my required treble on my 3rd dart. I've learned to keep myself calm(er) in games which has benefitted me in the long run.
improvements: Setups from the 300+ scores. Knowing when to move around the board to set yourself up appropriately for the next 3 darts.
dartSetup: Phoenix Custom barrels 22g, 6.5mm dia, 50mm long with Cosmo Standard #3 Locked Shafts and Cosmo Fit Flight Air Standard Flights
practiceRoutine: Focusing on finishes starting at 121 and moving up. If I miss I move down a number, if I succeed I move up. I also have a deck of cards with finishes from 170 down - I flip a card and give myself 6 darts to complete it. I struggle to practice alone so solo practice is 15-30 minutes. With a friend I can shoot for hours.
checkouts: A double is a double but I prefer a double that will break down (32/16/8/4/2/1). I am comfortable moving around the board and will take the route to the quickest finish.
currentForm: Very confident and pleased with my current performance. Aiming at building and improving focus and consistency.
recentResults: EAST COAST OPEN: 1st Place Mixed Doubles. 2nd Place Ladies Singles. 2nd Place Ladies Doubles with Ashley Foster. NS PROVINCIALS: 2nd Place. DEBBIE MULLIN MEMORIAL: Ladies Singles Joint 5th. 2025 World Masters in Budapest - nerves got the best of me but given the opportunity again I'll be ready!
mentalApproach: Calm, cool and collected at the oche. Sometimes humming a tune to keep it fun and positive.
pressureManagement: BREATHE! Just Breathe! I talk to myself, sometimes out loud, other times in my head. I stare the double down and make it mine.
stagePresence: Mostly focused on the board but using key people as focal points. I throw my darts and after each throw concentrate on my hands or flights and think about my next shot.
preMatchRituals: I don't believe I have any specific rituals, and if I do I'm not aware of them!
aadsMeaning: To be chosen as one of the first 10 women to be part of this inaugural event is truly an honor and I am humbled at this opportunity! It's a clear indication that I'm headed in the right direction.

introScript:
Ladies and gentlemen, representing New Brunswick…

He entered the Atlantic Amateur Darts Series as the final major test of Series 1.

A proven NDFC national-stage competitor and New Brunswick heavyweight, he came into Event 6 with serious credentials, including a strong round-robin performance at the NDFC Canadian Nationals and a perfect 5–0 group-stage run at the Debbie Mullin Memorial.

Then, in his AADS debut, with the final Tournament of Champions seat on the line, he won the whole event.

He is the late arrival, the final qualifier, and the man known as **The Final Boss**.

Ladies and gentlemen, make some noise for your **AADS Event 6 Champion**…

**Rob Sibbick!**
